speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me how old your child is and when these bleeding episodes first started? Also, has your child experienced any recent illnesses, fever, or unexplained bruising besides the nosebleeds and petechiae?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any other bleeding symptoms like blood in the stool or urine, and has the child had any recent infections or taken new medications? Does the family have any history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if your child has had any recent viral infections, and are there any other family members with similar bleeding problems? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Platelet Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Physical Exam: Diffuse petechiae on forearms, legs, and trunk; mild gum bleeding on probing; dried blood at nares. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 100/60 mmHg, Heart Rate 90 bpm, Respiratory Rate 20 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results confirm your child has Glanzmann's thrombasthenia, a rare bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency in the GIIb/IIIa receptors on platelets. Since the platelet count is normal but they cannot clump properly, this explains the mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia.
